author: ribeye
dek: A Cincinnati family got up before dawn for the Bengals' Madrid game — and for one terrifying minute, thought their TV had died in the final two minutes.
disclaimer: Parody: the Novak family of Cincinnati is fictional. The Bengals' win over the Falcons in Madrid is real, as reported by the Associated Press in November 2026.
headline: Cincinnati Family Watches Bengals Win in Madrid, Briefly Loses Power to Spain

ohio_quotes.quote: I spent forty dollars on coneys for a 9:30 game and I would do it again tomorrow. The dish towel matador cape is now a family heirloom.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Mike Novak, Cincinnati

ohio_quotes.quote: When the lights went out I thought our TV had finally given up. Then I realized the whole stadium in Madrid went dark, and honestly, that felt very on brand for this team.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Sarah Novak, Cincinnati

ohio_story: CINCINNATI, Ohio — Mike and Sarah Novak set two alarms for Sunday morning, which is not a sentence anyone in Cincinnati has ever said about a Bengals game before. Kickoff in Madrid was 9:30 a.m. Eastern, so the Novaks were up before the sun, the coffee was on by 8, and by kickoff their living room smelled like Skyline coneys, because Mike insists a Bengals game without coneys "doesn't count, even if it's breakfast, even if it's in Spain."

By the time Joe Burrow hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter, Mike had grabbed a dish towel and was doing his own matador cape routine in front of the television, while Sarah filmed it for the family group chat. Burrow kept dealing, Chase kept getting open, and Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns, and by halftime the Novaks were already debating whether a 9:30 a.m. kickoff should become a permanent tradition. "We have never been this awake for a Bengals game," Sarah said. "Usually I'm still negotiating with the remote at this hour."

Then, inside the final two minutes, the lights at the Bernabeu went out mid-play, and Sarah was certain their television had finally given up. Mike checked the breaker, the dog checked the couch, and then the picture came back and the down was replayed, and the Bengals closed out the 34-17 win anyway. The dish towel cape is now, Mike says, a family heirloom. The Novaks will be back on normal time next week, when the Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium — a game Mike has already decided requires coneys, too, "but at a normal hour, like a civilized person."
real_summary: Joe Burrow threw for three touchdowns and rushed for another, and the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, for their fourth straight win. The game was played at Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium.

Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards. Ja'Marr Chase had 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, including 142 yards in a career-high first half, and Tee Higgins added two touchdown catches. The Bengals scored on every possession before halftime, with three touchdowns and a field goal. After his 47-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, Chase celebrated with Higgins in bullfighting style, with Higgins mimicking a bull and Chase playing the matador with an imaginary cape.

The Bengals improved to 6-2 and have scored 30 points or more in four straight games for the first time since 1997, tying a franchise record. The Falcons fell to 3-6. A crowd of 78,660 was on hand, and the lights at the Bernabeu suddenly went out just as the Bengals were taking a snap inside the final two minutes, prompting the down to be replayed. It was the Bengals' first win in an international game, after tying Washington in 2016 and losing to the Los Angeles Rams in 2019, both times in London, and the second NFL regular-season game in Madrid.
source_note: AP recap carried by ESPN, Nov 2026: Bengals beat Falcons 34-17 in Madrid at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium.
